content.title: About
content.content: Ground pork is minced pork meat obtained from various cuts of the carcass, usually without bone or skin. Raw ground pork has a light pink color, soft texture, and the characteristic fresh meat aroma. It is used in cooking for making patties, sausages, sauces, fillings, and many other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground pork is a staple in traditional dishes worldwide, such as Russian kotleti, Italian ragù, and Asian stir‑fries with soy sauce.
Quality depends on the meat‑to‑fat ratio; an optimal fat content of 15‑20 % keeps the cooked product juicy.
Ground pork can be made from different parts—neck, shoulder, leg—each influencing flavor and texture.
Raw ground pork spoils quickly and should be kept at 0‑4 °C for no more than 1‑2 days.
In some countries pork mince is considered riskier than beef due to parasites, making thorough cooking essential.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune function, wound healing, and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Heme iron from pork is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw ground pork may harbor Salmonella, E. coli, and Trichinella; cook to an internal temperature of ≥ 71 °C.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Excess fat increases calorie density and may contribute to cardiovascular disease if consumed frequently.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: A small number of people can experience allergic reactions to pork.

items.title: Added sodium
items.content: Ground pork is often sold with added salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ground pork can be pan‑fried, stewed, baked, or boiled. Use it to form patties, meatballs, stuff vegetables, or add to sauces and soups. Before cooking, mix the meat thoroughly and season with herbs, onion, or garlic as desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw ground pork in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 1‑2 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C; it retains quality for 3‑4 months. Thaw frozen pork in the refrigerator, not at room temperature, before use.
